Paul / Olivia — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we have a shared checklist heading into the bench tests.

Recap (call highlights):
- StatCap cares mainly about 3 production properties: 1) consistent 99.9% availability for inference endpoints, 2) soft per-tenant rate limits that allow bursts (up to 5x baseline) without token loss, and 3) deterministic failover behavior across regions (no duplicate writes to downstream logging).
- You ran a short sample against MajorCloud’s hosted endpoint and saw a ~220ms p50 but a long tail at p99 (~1.9s) when load increased; pricing and token accounting were also a concern.
- StatCap would like an apples-to-apples SLO comparison and a small set of targeted stress tests to validate failover semantics.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) We'll provide a compact SLO comparison CSV that maps Redwood settings vs MajorCloud and HyperscaleX for the metrics above — attached.
2) Tech tests we suggest you run in your staging environment (we can execute with you):
   - Rate burst test: baseline 50 rps -> burst to 250 rps for 60s, observe throttling vs queueing and token loss.
   - Regional failover test: kill primary region A and verify single consistent stream to logging in region B with no duplicate events.
   - Long-tail probe: 1k concurrent short requests for 30m, measure p95/p99 and error budget burn.
3) We'll schedule a joint bench run next week (option: remote session where Camila drives the experiments).

Attachments: slo_comparison_table.csv (quick matrix), demo-recording.mp4 (call recording).

Open questions from our side:
- Do you have a preferred authentication model for the bench runs (API key vs temporary VPC token)?
- Any blackout windows for your staging environment this month?

If the above matches your expectations, I’ll lock the session for Tuesday AM PST and loop in Ethan to coordinate the data we’ll need.

Thanks,

Thanks — good notes. Adding a few technical clarifications and a suggested test harness (so the bench is reproducible).

Technical clarifications:
- Availability target: when we say 99.9% we mean successful 2xx responses for non-streaming generation calls over a rolling 30-day window; we can also provide metrics for streaming sessions separately.
- Rate limits: Redwood exposes per-API-key soft limits with a leaky-bucket enforcement. In practice bursts up to 5x are queued up to a configurable queue depth; only requests beyond that are rejected with 429. We will log exact queue-drops so you can assert token loss.
- Failover behavior: our regional handoff uses request idempotency keys + commit-log deduplication in the control plane to avoid duplicate event ingestion — this is why we can promise no duplicate downstream logs when a region fails.

Suggested test harness (Docker + k6 script):
- k6 scenario: baseline 50 rps for 10m -> spike to 250 rps for 60s -> back to 50 rps. Capture all response codes, server-side queue metrics (X-Redwood-Queue-Length), and token accounting headers.
- Failover: trigger a simulated region shutdown via our control endpoint (we can run in your staging account) and instrument the downstream logging pipeline to assert exactly-once for event ids.

I attached a compact CSV that templates the metrics we’ll capture (p50/p95/p99, 429 count, queue-drop count, error-budget burn). We can extend with additional columns if Olivia wants any product-side metrics included.

Let me know whether you prefer Redwood to run the harness or you want to run from StatCap’s side; either works. If StatCap will run it, we’ll provide the k6 script and a readme.

-Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
